titulo: Subjunctive: wishes, doubt and emotion: Wishes, requests and advice

aula.objetivo: Use the present subjunctive after verbs of wishing, asking and advising («quiero que vengas»), of doubt and denial («no creo que venga», «dudo que…») and of emotion and judgement («me alegra que…», «es importante que…»), and tell it apart from the indicative.

itens.pt: let's hope that, I hope that

blocos.titulo: Quiero que vengas: wanting someone else to do something
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: first, when to use it. If you want ANOTHER person to do something, the sentence has two subjects. English links them with an object + infinitive: "I want YOU TO COME". Spanish can't do that: it links the two with «que» and puts the second verb in the subjunctive: «Quiero que vengas» (literally "I want that you come"). STEP 2: when the subject is the SAME, there's no «que» and the second verb stays in the infinitive, as in English: «Quiero venir» (I want to come). STEP 3: verbs of wishing, asking, advising and influence that work this way: querer, desear, esperar, preferir, necesitar, pedir, aconsejar, recomendar, sugerir, exigir, permitir, prohibir, mandar, dejar. English "I need you to…", "I'd prefer you to…", "I'm asking you to…" all become «que» + subjunctive. STEP 4: «ojalá (que)» + subjunctive expresses a wish: «Ojalá llueva» (I hope it rains / let's hope it rains). STEP 5: with «aconsejar, permitir, prohibir, recomendar, dejar, pedir», when there's an indirect object, Spanish also accepts the infinitive, close to English: «Te aconsejo descansar» or «Te aconsejo que descanses» (I advise you to rest). Both are correct. STEP 6: «esperar que» means "to hope that", and here English uses the plain present, which tempts you into the indicative: "I hope you COME" = «Espero que VENGAS», never «espero que vienes». STEP 7: for the forms, use what you learned in lesson 42. STEP 8: in Latin America, «ustedes» replaces «vosotros»: «Quiero que vengan»; some regions also have their own «vos» forms.
blocos.comparacao: English "I want you to come", "I need you to help me", "I'd like you to stay" all use an object + infinitive. Spanish never does: «Quiero que vengas», «Necesito que me ayudes», «Me gustaría que te quedaras». And English "I hope you come" (plain present) is «Espero que vengas» — subjunctive. With only one subject, both languages use the infinitive: «Quiero venir».

tabela.exemplo: I'd prefer you to call me tomorrow.
I'm asking you to wait a moment.
I won't let you speak to me like that.
I want to rest for a while.

erros.motivo: After «querer que», the second verb goes in the subjunctive.
With the same subject, use the infinitive, with no «que» (as in English "I want to go").
«Esperar que» takes the subjunctive, even though English "I hope he comes" uses the present.
After «que», the verb has to be conjugated.

blocos.enunciado: Say five sentences with «quiero que… espero que… te pido que… te aconsejo que… ojalá…» about what you want from someone in your family or at work.
Say out loud the subjunctive of tener, hacer, ir, ser, estar and saber for «tú». Then conjugate «hablar» and «comer» for «yo» and «nosotros».
